submission.original_request: Create an executive Power BI sales-performance report. I need total sales, total orders, average order value and year-over-year sales. Show performance over time and let users filter by region, business area and product category. Include an executive summary and a detailed regional view. Use our corporate reporting standards.

original_schema.grain: One sales line per SaleId; an OrderId may contain multiple lines.

date_coverage.calendar: Gregorian, contiguous daily; complete two-year synthetic ledger; days without sales mean zero activity.

original_schema.null_policy: No nulls in baseline CSVs. Monetary values are nonnegative fixed two-decimal strings in CSV; quantities are positive integers.

answers.sales-definition: Net sales in AUD, SUM(FactSales.SalesAmount); DiscountAmount is a line-level discount already deducted.
answers.yoy-coverage: Use full calendar 2025 against 2024; both complete synthetic years are supplied. Outside coverage or with zero prior-year sales, return blank rather than inventing growth.
answers.region-security: Region is a slicer only in this golden case; no regional RLS is requested. A slicer is not security.

rules.text: Use SalesPerformance as the project name and Executive Summary / Regional Performance as the page names.
Use fictional theme Sales Demo: background #FFFFFF, text #172B4D, primary #005A9C. Do not convey meaning through colour alone.
Executive Summary must show Total Sales, distinct Total Orders, Average Order Value and Sales YoY %.
Use meaningful visual names and titles, readable labels, text alternatives and deliberate keyboard navigation. Actual accessibility verification remains pending.
Use the dedicated contiguous DimDate table for calendar-year comparisons; never fabricate missing prior-year values.
Prefer bar charts over pie/donut charts for regional and category comparisons.
Region is a filter, not access control. Do not claim RLS unless explicitly requested, implemented and runtime-tested.
Document local synthetic CSV inputs and unresolved deployment actions. Use TARGET_WORKSPACE_PLACEHOLDER rather than any real tenant, credential or endpoint.
